Hi Maria / team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful to hear the production constraints and the business KPI you're targeting for the triage assistant. Short recap + suggested path forward so we all have a concrete plan.

Key constraints you flagged:
- PHI touches in some user flows (claims intake) — this drives data residency and logging requirements.
- Extremely tight latency tolerance in the UI (goal: p50 sub-200ms for short prompts) for triage pages.
- Procurement wants an 8–10 week rollout cadence, but you want a 4-week PoC to validate fit prior to committing.

Deployment options (high level):
1) Hosted API (Redwood hosted): fastest to get started for functional validation, minimal onboarding. Less suitable if PHI cannot leave your VPC.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs in our cloud): gives you isolated capacity and predictable performance; easier to iterate than full VPC but requires networking configuration for secure traffic egress.
3) Private VPC/on-prem: full isolation & audit controls (KMS/HSM, custom network), matches strict PHI/regulatory controls but has longer setup time.

Proposed PoC timebox (4 weeks, goal: deployment decision at end):
- Week 0 (prep): security sync + MSA/SOW draft (procurement kickoff).
- Week 1: data integration + minimal end-to-end flow using non-PHI samples (smoke tests on Hosted or Dedicated).
- Week 2: performance baseline (latency/cost) on chosen mode (dedicated or private), KV cache and batching experiments.
- Week 3: tuning (quantization profile, batching, routing) and run acceptance prompts.
- Week 4: acceptance & decision (pass/fail acceptance criteria).

Success criteria (PoC acceptance):
- Functionality: 95% of critical prompts return acceptable outputs per your rubric (we'll sync rubric after this email).
- Performance: p50 latency < 200ms for 85% of acceptance prompts; p95 < 400ms under expected PoC concurrency.
- Cost guardrail: projected token cost delta within the budget threshold you shared (we'll calculate exact numbers once we have traces).
- Security: Redwood provides SOC2 attestation + network architecture that meets CardioLogic security team's requirements.

Proposed internal owners from Redwood:
- Marcus Lin (AE) — commercial/coordination, procurement lead.
- Camila Reyes (Solutions Eng) — technical lead for integration and PoC tests.
- Dylan Brooks (Customer Success) — post-PoC rollout planning and OKRs.

Action items for CardioLogic: 
1) Confirm whether CardioLogic will require Private VPC for the PoC (PHI in scope) or whether a Dedicated environment with a signed DPA and network controls would suffice for the 4-week timebox.
2) Confirm who on your side will own procurement (legal/procurement contact) and security (for SOC2/arch sync).
3) If Private VPC is required, please share the primary security contact and tentative dates for the security call this week.

I attached a short PoC charter and a deployment matrix that maps the workstreams + rough lead times. Also linking our SOC2 PDF in case your security team wants to review immediately.

Available for a 30–45m follow-up tomorrow afternoon if that helps.

Thanks,
Marcus

Hi Maria / Evan,

Thanks — looping in a few technical details that will help your security team triage quickly. Below is a minimal-setup architecture and the differences for each deployment mode.

Minimal architecture for PoC (high level):
- Ingress: CardioLogic app -> HTTPS -> Redwood ingress endpoint (PrivateLink / VPN / VPC peering as options). No PHI persisted in Redwood blob storage unless explicitly configured.
- Keys: Customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest (Private VPC option), Redwood-managed KMS for Hosted/Dedicated. We support customer KMS via AWS KMS grants + HSM integration for Private deployments.
- Logs & audit: API request logs (masked) shipped to your S3 bucket or to our secure log collector; retention configurable. Full audit trail available for VPC deployments.
- Network options:
  - Hosted API: easiest (no network setup). Not recommended for PHI.
  - Dedicated: isolated GPU pool with restricted egress + IP allowlist; can use PrivateLink for connections. Good tradeoff for a short PoC.
  - Private VPC: full private networking, customer-owned VPC peering or PrivateLink, customer KMS, strict audit logs. Best for long-term PHI workloads.

PoC acceptance tests (examples):
- Functional: run 200 representative prompts (mix of short triage prompts and longer context pushes) and measure output correctness against your rubric.
- Performance: run a concurrency test at expected PoC concurrency (we'll use a synthetic trace you provide) and measure p50/p95 latency and token throughput.
- Security: verify that logs are delivered to your S3 and that KMS key rotation policies are honored for a sample object.

Attachments I uploaded to the Drive link in Marcus' email: deployment_matrix.xlsx (maps tasks to owners and estimated lead times) and poc-charter.docx (scope, acceptance criteria, runbook). Also attaching our SOC2 PDF for immediate review.

Next steps I will take:
- Draft the 2-slide architecture sketch and drop it in the Drive by EOD today.
- Standby for the security sync calendar invite once Evan confirms availability.
- Provision a Dedicated PoC cluster as requested after procurement confirms the quick-order path.

If you prefer, we can run the initial functional validation on the Dedicated cluster within 48 hours of your greenlight — that will give you concrete latency and quality numbers while we work through the VPC onboarding.
